newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron plans LNG terminal in western India.
newsitem.headline: Enron plans LNG terminal in western India.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Enron Corp is setting up a five million tonne per year liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal in western India, a senior company official said on Thursday.
"Supply from the LNG terminal is expected to begin by middle of 2001," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Enron is negotiating a joint venture deal with the Qatar General Petroleum Corporation to set up a $5 billion project in Qatar to produce five million tonnes of LNG annually.

"Our main focus is now on the Indian market which, we think, can absorb large amounts of gas," Kelly Kimberly, spokeswoman for the Houston-based corporation, told Reuters on the sidelines of a gas conference in the Qatari capital Doha on Wednesday.

Two million tonnes of the planned output would go to fuel a 2,450-megawatt power plant Enron is building at Dabhol in the western Indian state of Maharashtra and one million tonnes annually to Gujarat Gas Corporation, with which it has signed a memorandum of understanding, Kimberly said.
"We have the approval for a LNG terminal at Dabhol for our power project," the Enron official in New Delhi said.
Work on the Dabhol power plant resumed late last year after the ruling Hindu nationalist government in Maharashtra renegotiated a contract it had said was too expensive.
Enron has invited offers from firms willing to enter into a long-term contract for supply of LNG. "The parties will have a 25-year contract with a take-or-pay clause," the official said.
"The price of the gas to customers is expected to be lower than the delivered price of imported naphtha."
The company plans to build a pipeline from Dabhol to Surat in neighbouring Gujrat state.

This will allow Enron to link its LNG gas feed with state-owned Gas Authority of India Ltd's existing HBJ (Hazira-Bijapur-Jagdishpur) gas pipeline grid, transporting gas from the western coast to north India, for supplying to customers in different states, the official said.
"We could use the HBJ pipeline. Looping could also be done to the HBJ pipeline," he said.
On Tuesday, the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu announced that it had awarded a multi-million-dollar contract to Enron to build a 242-megawatt power plant.

Enron's Dabhol Power Company (DPC) was one of eight fast track projects designed to lure foreign private investment into India's crumbling infrastructure sector shortly after open market reforms were launched in 1991.
